newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai's unemployment rate up 20 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai's unemployment rate up 20 percent in 1996.

text.p: The number of Shanghai's unemployed workers, including staff placed on subsistence wages by bankrupt state enterprises, rose 20 percent during 1996, the city's statistical bureau chief said on Wednesday.

The problem of "xiagang" workers -- staff of state enterprises forced out of their jobs with only a small living allowance -- was one of the biggest problems currently facing China's largest city, Sun Zuyao told a news conference.
He said the number of people in the city registered as unemployed with no connection to any work unit was 150,000 at the end of 1996, about the same as at the end of 1995.
But he said the number of "xiagang" workers had risen to 270,000 by the end of 1996, up from 200,000 at the end of 1995.

Analysts say China's communist government forces the heavily-indebted state enterprises to keep most of their workers on their books, fearing the social consequences of sudden and massive unemployment.
